member: Marcus - Vibration Control and Damping Specialist
message:
Elena, Priya, Tomas, proposal is hidden under-deck vertical Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, secondary sprung mass plus dampers tuned to bridge mode) at midspan on bolted clamp frame with staged night install plus re-tuning access. Plainly small extra weight tames bus-scale deck motion; numbers are modal stiffness calculation (E11) with 20000 kg, about 286 body weights, giving 2.85 MN per m at 1.90 Hz, and Den Hartog optimum re-check (E54) with 500 kg tuned to 1.85 Hz at 0.0956 damping ratio.

Dense crowd would throw people; damper gives gentle braking, inside comfort. Plainly violent to comfortable; numbers are dense-crowd resonant force estimate (E50) of 1480 N giving bare-deck acceleration scaling (E51) of 9.26 m per s squared, 0.944 times gravity and outside footbridge experience so linear resonance overpredicts, versus TMD-controlled acceleration scaling (E52) of 0.545 m per s squared, 0.0556 times gravity, below 1.00 m per s squared minimum bound in Experimental and Numerical Study on Dynamics of Two Footbridges (E38).

Unit stays clear and buildable below deck. Plainly thumbnail motion with car-scale frame load; numbers are dense-crowd stroke scaling (E53) of 20.1 mm with 2.49 times margin to plus-minus 50 mm stops in bolted frame sketch (E37), carrying TMD weight calculation (E35) of 4.90 kN under factored frame design load (E36) of 12.3 kN. Ready, because load, clearance, comfort and access close jointly.
